context: Isaac, 2026-11-05: position WOTR as a medieval world, toward what he already writes.

batch1.headline: Its own words, touchstones after: 'A medieval world that runs on old magic: lethal courts, deep and frightening powers, and fighters who shout their techniques across the battlefield.' For feel: Final Fantasy's world, Martin's politics, Tolkien's sense of age, anime's heat.
batch1.eras: His words: Medieval for the most part, however we could have the Imperial Age be like the turn of the century in the Renaissance era, which was right after the Dark Ages.
batch1.guns: No guns; crossbows take over: firearms leave the setting; a crossbow bolt becomes the cheap weapon that can kill a high-Stage fighter in a room.
batch1.magic_infrastructure: His words: Magic is everywhere, but a mixture of Final Fantasy and Tolkien; old works and old stuff exist from the Great Spirit War and the days when the Physical Epochs existed, like Bara, Ashura and Aegor in their human form.

batch2.imperial_place: His words: this storyline right now is about the Dark Ages, around three arcs long with three main villains, and most of the characters get to see the turn of the century.

batch3.fame_without_print: Criers, ballads, bounty boards: heralds cry the news, minstrels spread songs that get details wrong, lords post bounties, bookies still take odds.
batch3.daily_magic_source: Living people and their crafts: guild craftsmen, hedge-workers and petty folk arts; magic is a trade people do with their hands, so it costs money and someone can refuse.
batch3.draw_vocabulary: His words: get rid of the idea of the draw, since most practitioners don't even use it; they pull from the magic that literally exists in the environment. Go back to a more cultivation approach.
batch3.three_villains: His words: Malphas and the Sins, then Cozbi, then Kujo.

batch4.cultivation_model: His words: most Aether is pulled from the environment, and Aethers can have different types and affect your Soul Crystal differently, aka Wellsprings; these Wellsprings are sources of power; they also represent alchemical principles but also spiritual transformations; this is how it worked before in older lore.
batch4.power_rarity: Practitioners are common too: closer to shonen; fighters and cultivators are all over, with sects and ranks everyone knows.
batch4.mystery_vs_explained: Everything explained eventually: scholars have an account of everything, even the gods; it may be wrong, and a Measurewright will argue about it.
batch4.split_placement: Near the end of Arc 1: Arc 1 Malphas and the Sins, in the Grand World, ending as Malakar breaks it; Arc 2 Cozbi, in the ruins; Arc 3 Kujo, and the turn of the century.

batch5.old_scenes: Revise scenes now: 'the draw' lines become Aether in every affected scene file.
batch5.martin_deaths: Sudden in politics, fair in fights: betrayals, poison and assassinations can kill major NPCs with no warning as long as the clues were on the page; fights keep their findable way out.
batch5.law_timing: Now, adjust as we go: write R83 and update Natalie now, then redo the pilot under both before any more cards change.
